findings.summary: Event-file cleanup relies only on `defer os.Remove(path)` inside Emacsclient.Deliver, and the CLI installs no signal handling. If a parent harness sends SIGINT/SIGTERM while emacsclient is still running, the process can exit before the deferred remove runs, leaving a 0600 imoogi-agent-*.json in TMPDIR. The ACs only list the internal --timeout case, which is covered, so this is outside their stated scenarios.

The receiver does not check who owns the event file or its mode. Plan D-10 accepts that the server may read the file late, after the CLI has timed out and deleted it. On a shared, world-writable TMPDIR (the Linux default /tmp when TMPDIR is unset), another local user could recreate a file with the same name in that window. The receiver would then process that user's JSON as a genuine event. This works around the spec's premise that 'the default socket is user-only, so other users cannot send events'. The impact is limited to message, open-file, goto and notice actions on files the victim can already read; no code runs. On this macOS host the per-user TMPDIR is drwx------, which blocks it. Possible fix: check that file-attribute-user-id equals (user-uid) and that the file is not group- or world-writable, or have the CLI create a private 0700 subdirectory.

findings.summary: When EMACSCLIENT is a bare name (no slash), the CLI resolves it against the current working directory with filepath.Abs and runs ./<name>. REQ-AIPC-013 says discovery matches scripts/imoogi-editor, but that script's `exec "${emacsclient}"` looks a slash-less name up in PATH. So in the one case both accept, the Go CLI can run an executable planted in the agent's working directory, such as an untrusted repo. This is the hazard Go's exec.ErrDot exists to prevent. The comment on line 125 shows it is deliberate, and a test pins it. It needs the user to set EMACSCLIENT to a bare name, so it is minor. Possible fix: use exec.LookPath for slash-less values, or reject them.

Nothing limits the size of the payload file the receiver opens. The 1 MiB cap applies only to the event itself. imoogi-agent--visit sets large-file-warning-threshold to nil and calls find-file-noselect directly. So an open-file, goto-location, artifact-created or task-finished event naming a multi-GB regular file makes the Emacs server read the whole file into memory. That can freeze the user's editor well past the CLI's 5 s timeout. AC-010 requires suppressing the prompt, not removing every bound; a hard cap that rejects oversized files, such as error:too-large, would keep the no-prompt rule.

findings.summary: Leftover-data hygiene: the event file is removed only by a deferred call in Deliver, and the CLI installs no signal handler. If the calling agent's harness sends SIGINT or SIGTERM mid-delivery (for example, a cancelled tool call), the file stays in TMPDIR. The file is mode 0600 and, on macOS, sits in a per-user directory; SIGKILL can never be handled anyway. The spec's list of 'every path' (success, reject, delivery failure, timeout) does not mention signals, so this is hygiene rather than a spec violation.

findings.summary: Dependency injection is done two different ways. Deps injects Getenv and Getwd so request parsing is testable. emacsclient discovery ignores Deps: it reads os.Getenv("EMACSCLIENT") and os.Getenv("EMACS_VERSION") directly, and tests override the mutable package global appBundleCandidates. findings.summary: The two helper-process fake emacsclients in the same SPEC follow different conventions. They use different env var names (IMOOGI_AGENT_FAKE_MODE/IMOOGI_AGENT_FAKE_RECORD vs IMOOGI_AGENT_TEST_FAKE_MODE/IMOOGI_AGENT_TEST_FAKE_MARKER), a different trigger env, a different accept-mode token ("ok" vs ""), different helper names (useFake vs useFakeEmacsclient) and different record structs (Argv0 in only one). Go cannot share unexported test helpers across packages, so some duplication is structural. The naming and token drift is not forced by that.

Transport.Deliver takes `timeout time.Duration` and creates its own context from context.Background(). Sibling packages that run subprocesses or block (internal/setup, internal/fetch, internal/orgpreview, internal/anki/planner) take a caller-supplied context.Context, and no sibling function takes a timeout Duration parameter. This also differs from the repo Go rule 'Use context.Context as first parameter for functions that may block'. Behaviour is correct; the API shape differs from its neighbours.

This is history metadata, not code style, and it does not affect the score. The SPEC's M4 commit carries a placeholder author identity, unlike every other commit in recent history. The cause is traced to an unrelated provenance-test git env leak into .git/config during the pre-commit hook, fixed later in 43f88d1. It is not fixable without rewriting pushed history.

evidence_gaps.gap: AC-015 real Emacs 30.2 daemon smoke test was NOT run. It spawns daemons and sockets, which is outside read-only scope. Expected results are exit=0 message, exit=3 bad-path, exit=3 not-loaded, exit=1 no socket, and no leftover event file. The only record of these is a self-report in .moai/specs/SPEC-AGENTIPC-001/progress.md:106 ('smoke_emacs_30_2: exit=0 | exit=3 bad-path | exit=3 not-loaded | exit=1 ...'). Partial support: a batch probe of the exact evalExpr in real Emacs 30.2 with server-eval-args-left bound gave: P1 not-loaded: "error:not-loaded" left=nil; P2 loaded+missing file: "error:unreadable" left=nil; P3 loaded+non-JSON file: "error:parse". The emacsclient-to-server transport itself was not exercised.

AC-015 `make build-agent && test -x bin/imoogi-agent` was not run literally, to avoid writing into the repo's bin/ (currently absent and gitignored: `.gitignore:29:/bin/ bin/imoogi-agent`). Substitutes that were run: `make -n build-agent` printed 'mkdir -p bin / go build -o bin/imoogi-agent ./cmd/imoogi-agent' with exit=0. `go build -o $SCRATCH/imoogi-agent ./cmd/imoogi-agent && test -x ...` gave 'build+test-x exit=0'. The built binary printed 'imoogi-agent dev' (exit 0) for --version, exited 1 for a non-executable EMACSCLIENT, and exited 2 for 'finish done'.

AC-003(c) on a file WITHOUT a trailing newline was verified only by reading the code: goto point-max, then move-to-column measured from line start. No such tracked file existed to probe, and creating one would violate read-only scope. The ERT test covers only a file with a trailing newline.

AC-009's full rejection list (relative, missing, dir, symlink-dir, dangling, /dev/null, TRAMP) is exercised only for open-file. goto-location, artifact-created and task-finished are tested only with the missing-path case. They share imoogi-agent--resolve-paths, so the policy is uniform by construction, but that uniformity was checked by reading the code rather than by running each rejection case.

Read-only mode ruled out creating an on-disk symlink to a TRAMP path. That case was simulated in memory by advising file-symlink-p on a fake path. In both TRAMP states (preloaded, and not preloaded with the recorder hooked via with-eval-after-load 'tramp-sh) the receiver returned error:bad-path and tramp-maybe-open-connection was never called. The positive control (file-exists-p on /ssh:nonexistent.invalid:/etc/hosts) did record OPEN-CONNECTION, so the probe is valid. A real on-disk symlink was not exercised.

The late-read substitution race (finding 1) was not reproduced. It needs a multi-user Linux host with a shared /tmp and file creation, neither of which was available. The finding rests on code reading, plan D-10 and the TMPDIR permissions shown.

The EMACSCLIENT cwd-binary case (finding 2) was not executed, because that needs a planted ./emacsclient file. The behavior is shown by the source and by the existing test TestAC14DiscoveryIgnoresDirectoriesAndRelativePath.

Only Emacs 30.2 was used for probes; server-eval-args-left behavior on Emacs 31.1 was not run. Emacs older than 30.1 (no server-eval-args-left, so the path argument might be evaluated) is out of scope in the spec and was not tested.
The AC-015 real-daemon smoke test (exit codes against a live Emacs server, event-file cleanup after timeout) was not run.

Side effects of visiting non-text payload files were not exercised: jka-compr running gzip, doc-view running Ghostscript, vc-refresh-state running git in the payload's repo, and deferred eglot-ensure starting language servers. These come from the environment and config, not from the receiver itself.

Tests run and passing: `go test ./cmd/imoogi-agent/... ./internal/agentipc/... -count=1` gave 'ok ... cmd/imoogi-agent 9.321s' and 'ok ... internal/agentipc 2.430s'.
